No, patients with diabetes may not always receive the same message from dietitians and nurses. While both healthcare professionals play a crucial role in diabetes management, their areas of expertise and communication styles may vary, potentially leading to inconsistent advice. 

Dietitians typically provide detailed, personalized nutrition counseling, focusing on meal planning, carbohydrate counting, and healthy eating habits. Nurses, on the other hand, may offer more general guidance on diabetes management, including medication adherence, blood glucose monitoring, and overall self-care.

To ensure consistent messaging, it's essential for dietitians and nurses to collaborate and communicate effectively, providing patients with a unified and comprehensive approach to diabetes care.
